description: Soil Deep Drainage Potential is a dataset listed in South Australian Government data directory (data.sa.gov.au), Australia, an open data portal, published or maintained by Department for Environment and Water. Deep drainage refers to the capacity of the deep subsoil and the material immediately below the soil profile to allow excess water to move downwards into deep sediments or fractured rock. Poorly structured or heavy clays are the most restrictive. Coverage: South Australia. The portal files it under the publisher Department for Environment and Water. Its tags are agriculture, land use, soil, soil and land attribute data, soil attributes. It offers 6 resource(s) in geojson, html, kmz, pdf, shp. The portal shows 2020-02-18 as the last metadata change. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is Creative Commons Attribution. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support urban drainage and flood-risk studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-ditrdcsa-data-sa.
